transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Claire Huang (Redwood AE), Danny Park (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (LumenScale VP Platform), Maya Ortiz (LumenScale SRE Lead), Ethan Wu (LumenScale FinOps)

00:00 - Claire: okay cool thanks everyone for making time, we're calling this the mid-year health + economics touchpoint, um we wanted to go through the usage spikes you flagged and then walk through a stability playbook that maps to the two services you mentioned.
00:18 - Raj: yep thanks Claire, quick note on timing, we've got end-of-month review with leadership so looking to lock decisions this week if possible.
00:26 - Maya: and I wanted to make sure we carved out time to talk about the incident last week where latency spiked for recommendation-api, looked like queueing at the model side.
00:38 - Danny: yeah I pulled some traces, there was an increased prompt length and a KV cache miss pattern. I'm thinking a small prefix cache and fallbacks to a lower-cost quantized variant would help.
00:52 - Ethan: cost is the other side of that, our token bill is up 34% q/q, a lot of it coming from chat-like sessions and the long-context agents. We're exploring dedicated vs hosted reserved to get predictability.
01:10 - Claire: totally. For pricing we've got three levers — batch/caching, reserved capacity (Dedicated), and quantized model variants. We'll send a detailed breakdown after this call.
01:22 - Raj: can you show concrete numbers? like break down per-endpoint cost if we moved 50% of traffic to Dedicated?
01:31 - Claire: yes that's in the follow-up sheet, but high level Dedicated reduces unit GPU cost on sustained throughput, while Hosted gives burst elasticity — there's a breakpoint depending on steady qps.
01:45 - Maya: our SLO for recommendation-api is p95 < 120ms, and for content-filter it's p95 < 80ms. Can Dedicated meet that?
01:55 - Danny: it can, if we tune batching windows and avoid large batch tail latencies. Also need to configure KV cache for hot prefixes; that cuts tokens and latency.
02:07 - Raj: what about fallbacks for regional outages? We don't want full failover to a slow model.
02:13 - Danny: we recommend a fallback chain — primary low-latency model, then a quantized model in same region, then cross-region fallback only as last resort. Also automatic rollback on anomaly detection.
02:29 - Ethan: talk to me about burst vs reserve math — we need to know payback on reserved commit in 3–6 months.
02:36 - Claire: we'll run a scenarios sheet. For example, a 3-month 500k token/day steady commit shows X% unit cost reduction — I'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
02:48 - Raj: have you guys run our test corpus? we want apples-to-apples latency numbers.
02:53 - Danny: not yet with your corpus — we proposed a bench earlier but didn't get the traffic dump. We should run Hosted and Dedicated with same sequence length distribution and tail tokens.
03:05 - Maya: I'll send a sanitized sample. Also note we have encryption at rest rules and KMS needs to be customer-managed for production.
03:13 - Claire: Redwood Private supports customer KMS — we'll include that in docs.
03:18 - Raj: and SOC2 evidence — our procurement needs to see SOC2 Type II and network architecture.
03:23 - Claire: we have SOC2 Type II attestation, plus a network diagram for VPC peering and private control plane — will attach.
03:31 - Ethan: what about observability — token-level cost attribution, per-route SLO dashboards? we need cost by product line.
03:38 - Danny: Redwood Console has token-level breakdown and per-route lat/err dashboards; we can show filtered views in the demo.
03:46 - Maya: we sometimes see spikes from a small number of heavy users, is there rate-limiting?
03:51 - Claire: yes per-route quotas and token-rate limits; we can propose policies and exception processes.
04:00 - Raj: on the playbook, what are the exact steps if we see a degradation — who does what?
04:07 - Danny: proposed playbook: 1) detect anomaly via Console alert, 2) if it's cache cold, pre-warm prefixes, 3) if latency persists, route to quantized variant, 4) if region capacity constrained, spill to reserved Dedicated in same region, 5) if all else fails, circuit-break to degraded-mode responses. We'll document runbooks and handlers.
04:34 - Maya: can you pre-author the runbook steps so our on-call can run without Redwood SE? we want runbook automation.
04:40 - Danny: yes we'll provide runbook docs and a checklist for on-call play.
04:44 - Ethan: back to pricing, can you model a hybrid — reserved base for 70% with 30% burst in Hosted?
04:50 - Claire: yes that's a common pattern, we'll include cost curves for those mixes.
04:55 - Raj: competitor question — we've had inbound from Anthropic and OpenAI — what differentiates Redwood on reliability and ops?
05:03 - Claire: our emphasis is production controls: unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, KV caching, and tooling for rollouts and tracing. Also SLO-driven routing and transparent benchmarks.
05:15 - Maya: any gotchas for private deployments? networking or air-gapped restrictions?
05:20 - Danny: you need to plan for image updates and offline model syncs; HSM/KMS integration can add lead time but we have a playbook for that.
05:30 - Raj: okay can we agree next steps?
05:34 - Claire: recap — Redwood will: (1) send pricing permutations + scenarios, (2) attach SOC2 + network diagram, (3) schedule bench for Hosted vs Dedicated with LumenScale corpus. LumenScale will: (a) send traffic sample, (b) confirm two critical endpoints and SLOs, (c) review internal procurement timeline.
05:58 - Ethan: thanks all — we'll aim to make a decision by 2026-07-31.
06:05 - Claire: great; Danny and I will follow up with calendar invites and deliverables. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: occasional hypos, speaker IDs auto-attributed, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (kv cache sometimes as K-V cash), natural cross-talk at 02:29 and 04:34.

Referenced artifacts: pricing workbook (link: /redwood/pricing/LumenScaleQ3.xlsx), SOC2 attestation (link: /redwood/compliance/soc2.pdf), network diagram (link: /redwood/diagrams/lumenscale-network.png), bench proposal doc (link: /redwood/bench/lumenscale-bench.md).
